prompt:
You are the SCAFFOLDER (opus) in an autonomous substrate-build loop. You build a generic, reusable Lean substrate module.

## Requirement
# Substrate requirement: finite-side-information-minimax-convergence

## Goal
Build axiom-clean reusable finite decision-theory substrate proving convergence from empirical finite side information to an exactly observed side-law vector.

## Provides (API contract)
- `finiteSideInfo_minimax_tendsto`: for a compact parameter space, finite labeled and nonempty side alphabets, continuous probability coordinates, and a continuous bounded real target, the bounded squared-loss minimax values based on labeled data plus `m` iid side observations tend as `m → ∞` to the benchmark minimax value based on the labeled data plus the exact side-law vector.
- A compact coordinate-simplex representation for probability mass functions on a finite type, with continuous atom coordinates and continuous finite product probabilities.
- Continuity and boundedness lemmas for finite squared risks.
- Specialization lemmas for a parameter space that is a closed subset of a finite simplex.

## Statement / milestones
Let `Theta` be compact, `X` a finite labeled alphabet, and `C` a finite nonempty side alphabet. Let `p : Theta → X → Real` and `q : Theta → C → Real` be continuous probability coordinates and let `tau : Theta → Real` be continuous and bounded. Define the bounded squared-loss minimax value when the procedure observes the labeled outcome together with `m` iid draws from `q theta`, and the benchmark value when it instead observes the exact vector `q theta`. Prove that the former tends along `Nat.atTop` to the latter.

The proof must supply the full reusable chain: exact-`q` simulation and squared-loss conditional averaging for the lower comparison; compact shrinking-fiber local-minimax convergence; finite-cover approximate decision selection measurable in the empirical side vector; a uniform finite-category empirical L1 tail from Hoeffding and a union bound; and the liminf/limsup assembly.

## Standard reference
Standard compact statistical decision theory: comparison of experiments, Rao–Blackwell conditional averaging under convex squared loss, compactness/finite-cover arguments, and finite-alphabet empirical concentration via Hoeffding. No paper-specific theorem may be assumed.

## Intended reuse
The immediate consumer is the known-marginal limiting theorem in `stat_semisupervised_discrete_ate_annotation_frontier/v1`. The shared declarations must remain paper-independent. The run-local specialization will encode its discrete-law coordinates, closed overlap-constrained model class, ATE continuity at null cells, finite-sum risks, and auxiliary empirical table.

## May assume / must derive
May assume compactness of `Theta`, finiteness/nonemptiness of the alphabets, continuity and probability-simplex validity of `p` and `q`, and continuity/boundedness of `tau`. Must derive the PMF simplex compactness/continuity API, risk continuity, shrinking-fiber minimax interchange, measurable finite-cover selector, exact-side comparison, empirical L1 concentration, and convergence theorem. All public results must have zero `sorry`, use no `admit`, and introduce no axioms.

## Non-goals (optional)
Do not import any `CausalSmith/*_Research` module. Do not encode the paper's `DiscreteLaw`, overlap inequalities, `ateFunctional`, `auxTableOf`, or annotation experiment; those are run-local prerequisites and specializations after promotion. Do not weaken the main result to a conditional gate or one-sided bound.

## Known building blocks (optional)
Search and reuse `Causalean.Stat.Minimax.FiniteSquaredLoss.Core`, `Causalean.Stat.Minimax.MinimaxValue`, `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.TailBounds.Hoeffding`, `Causalean.Stat.FiniteSquaredLoss.isCompact_procedureSet`, `Causalean.Stat.FiniteSquaredLoss.continuous_rawRisk`, `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.hoeffding_abs_ge`, `Mathlib.Probability.ProbabilityMassFunction.Constructions`, `Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.Compact`, and `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic`. Generic `ProbabilityTheory.minimaxRisk` and Hoeffding alone do not already provide the required compact-fiber minimax interchange.


## Workspace
- Write/extend Lean files under: <repo-root>/CausalSmith/CausalSmith/Substrate/FiniteSideInformationMinimaxConvergence
- Module prefix (one file per module): CausalSmith.Substrate.FiniteSideInformationMinimaxConvergence.<Name>
- This is build round 1 of at most 10.

## Your task this turn
0. ASSESS CURRENT STATUS FROM GROUND TRUTH. You are a fresh invocation with NO memory of prior turns — your only context is this prompt plus what you read from disk. Read the current files under the Lean dir and check their real state (remaining `sorry`s and any errors) via lean-lsp diagnostics or a targeted build. Trust the files over the prior round report (a report can lag a partial filler edit). The report and your prior plan below tell you the INTENT; the files tell you the TRUTH.
1. Search the existing library FIRST (run `npm run search -- "<concept>"` in CausalSmith/tools; use lean-lsp local/leansearch) to reuse, not reinvent.
1b. FETCH THE PRIMARY SOURCE when possible. If the Requirement names a reference (or you find the canonical one), fetch it to ground the exact statement, hypotheses, and naming/conventions you formalize — via WebFetch/WebSearch or Bash `curl`/`wget`; for an arXiv paper download the LaTeX source and read the `.tex`, not the PDF. Skip only when no source is named or none is reachable; never block on it.
2. UPDATE `plan_markdown` as a STRUCTURED STATUS LEDGER (this IS the memory the next turn inherits — make it concrete, not a vision doc). Use these sections: `## Done` (decls proven/closed), `## Remaining` (the open sorries, by file), `## Blocked` (what's stuck and why), `## Decisions` (design/API choices + what was tried and rejected, so the next turn doesn't repeat dead ends). Keep it CONCISE — bullet points referencing decl/file names, NOT full proof derivations. Per-lemma proof strategy and tactic sketches belong in the Lean file as docstrings/comments (you write those to disk directly), not duplicated into this JSON string.
3. WRITE or EXTEND the Lean scaffold: precise statements with `sorry` for unproven proofs. The file(s) MUST compile with only `sorry` warnings (no hard errors). Keep each file focused, normally ≤600 lines; split before ~900 only for an independent topic/proof chain. Include a `/-! -/` module docstring and a docstring on each public declaration (first paragraph = self-contained NL translation).
3b. KEEP THE DEPENDENCY LAYER CLEAN. Staging files may import Mathlib, Causalean, and other files under this run's own `CausalSmith.Substrate.FiniteSideInformationMinimaxConvergence` tree. Never import a paper/research module or any other CausalSmith run. If a needed reusable prerequisite exists only in a paper folder, escalate instead of importing or copying it; main must extract it into this same temporary tree first.
4. DECIDE how many codex subagents to use to fill the sorries this round, and emit ONE prompt per subagent (partition the sorries as you judge best).
4b. DECOMPOSE BEFORE RETRYING. A single `sorry` may hide several independent research-scale
obligations. If one filler reports two or more substantive blockers, or the same target returns
unchanged in two rounds, do not issue that monolithic target again. First add focused helper
declarations/modules for the smallest dependency-ordered obligations, with honest `sorry`s, and
dispatch only the lowest open import layer. A later filler may target the headline only after those
helpers are closed. Repeating the same prompt with more detail is not decomposition. Missing
infrastructure, expected formalization effort, or the remaining round budget is not by itself an
escalation reason; escalate only with concrete evidence that the contract is false/inconsistent or
would require a forbidden dependency.

## Integrity (HARD RULES — non-negotiable)
- Do NOT LAUNDER. Never weaken, narrow, or special-case a statement, and never delete or relax a hypothesis that should be proven, just to make the build pass or satisfy the reviewer. The statements must stay the genuine, general results the Requirement asks for. Strengthening an assumption to dodge a hard case, replacing the real goal with a corollary, or hiding the difficulty in a definition all count as laundering — do not do it.
- Do NOT create VACUOUS statements. No trivially-true claims, no `True`-like lemmas, no uninhabitable/contradictory hypotheses, no premises that are never satisfiable (an always-false hypothesis makes any conclusion hold for free). Every theorem must have real content and be applicable to the intended inhabited inputs.
- When revising after a failed review, FIX THE PROOF / API — not the goalposts. Address the findings without diluting what the module proves.
- If a clean, true, non-vacuous statement is genuinely out of reach, choose decision="escalate" with the reason. Escalating is correct; laundering or shipping a vacuous statement is a failure.

## Decisions
- decision="build": you wrote/updated the scaffold and want the fillers to run this round. Provide `codex_prompts` (>=1).
- decision="review": choose this ONLY after you have VERIFIED from ground truth that the module compiles with ZERO remaining sorries and zero errors (confirm via diagnostics/build this turn — do not infer it from the report) AND the statements are the genuine, non-vacuous results (no laundering). `codex_prompts` may be empty.
- decision="escalate": the goal is wrong, unrealistic, or only reachable by weakening it into something vacuous; set `escalation.reason`. The run halts.

Emit ONLY the StructuredOutput JSON object: { decision, plan_markdown, codex_prompts: [{id, target_decls, prompt}], escalation? }.
`plan_markdown` is your living status ledger (persisted to plan.md and fed back to you next turn) — keep it accurate.
KEEP THE WHOLE EMITTED JSON COMPACT (target: a few KB, not tens of KB). Detailed proof strategy, Lean snippets, and long derivations go in the Lean files on disk (docstrings/comments) and in FOCUSED per-sorry `codex_prompts` — never as a bulk dump inside `plan_markdown`. A very large structured emit can corrupt the tool-call encoding, so a bounded emit is a correctness requirement, not just style.
